points.text: (electrostatic) attraction between nuclei of two atoms and shared pair of electrons
M1: $\sigma$ bond – diagram showing how $\sigma$ bond is made from direct overlap of orbitals
M2: $\pi$ bond – diagram showing how $\pi$ bond is made from sideways overlap of $2\times$ p-orbitals
EITHER (pair of) electrons in $\pi$ bond are further away from the nuclei so weaker attraction OR (pair of) electrons in $\sigma$ bond are closer to the two nuclei so stronger attraction
M1: arrow from = of $\text{C=C}$ to H of $\text{H-Br}$
M2: correct dipole on $\text{H-Br}$ as $\delta+\text{H}-\text{Br}^{\delta-}$ AND arrow from $\text{H-Br}$ bond to Br
M4: arrow from lone pair on $\text{Br}^-$ to $\text{C}^+$ of their intermediate (with +ve or $\delta+$ charge)
